AbstractText.Label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To assess the feasibility and safety of a McCall culdoplasty at time of total laparoscopic hysterectomy and to evaluate differences in total vaginal length, vaginal apex during valsalva, and sexual function 12 months after McCall culdoplasty compared to standard cuff closure.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Pilot randomized controlled, single masked trial (Canadian Task Force classification I) SETTING: Academic tertiary care hospital PATIENTS: Women undergoing total laparoscopic hysterectomy for benign indications from June 2013 to December 2013.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: Women were randomized (1:1) to McCall culdoplasty followed by standard cuff closure versus standard cuff closure. Patients underwent Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) exam and completed the Female Sexual Function Index immediately prior to surgery, and at 6 months and 12 months postoperatively. Primary outcome was operative time. Secondary outcomes included estimated blood loss, complications, total vaginal length, vaginal apex during valsalva, and sexual function.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: This study included 50 patients. The groups were similar in terms of preoperative and surgical characteristics. Operative time did not differ between the groups. Estimated blood loss and complications were also similar. Loss to follow up was similar in both groups. Change in total vaginal length, vaginal apex during valsalva, sexual function, and pain with intercourse did not differ between the groups.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: In this pilot study, the addition of McCall culdoplasty to standard cuff closure during total laparoscopic hysterectomy was not associated with increase in operative time, estimated blood loss, or surgical complications. No differences in total vaginal length or vaginal apex during valsalva were seen at 12-month follow-up. There were no differences in sexual dysfunction or dyspareunia. Given the well-established risk reduction for development of apical prolapse with McCall culdoplasty during vaginal hysterectomy, this procedure may be a feasible and safe addition to total laparoscopic hysterectomy.
